Merge pull request #176 from 0xshikhar/fix/hardening-and-protocol-v2

Hardening + protocol v2: content-bound signatures, node deploy readiness, worker/web security
docs: Add commit and PR conventions for project contributors
feat(node): Include canonical edge resolver in Tor/IPFS gateway race

feat(tor): Configure live AWS Fargate Tor v3 .onion address across all surfaces

- Point default .onion host across web, worker, node, SDK CLI, browser
  extension, publish-action, and WordPress plugin to the persistent Tor v3
  hidden service running on AWS ECS Fargate + EFS (ap-southeast-2):
  6wst2skhjdkaltwvy37clw2mzk75lteq66qu5qzg3ujhresdhloy63yd.onion
- Bind Tor SocksPort to 127.0.0.1:9050 inside the container and initialize
  all /data subdirectories on EFS mount
- Add AGENTS.md with AWS Agent Toolkit configuration for ap-southeast-2
sec(node): Use scrypt KDF for API key hashing to resolve CodeQL alert #88
ci: Pass toolchain: stable to pinned dtolnay/rust-toolchain action

fix: Restore .onion routing, ensure backwards compatibility, and resolve CodeQL/CI alerts

- Restore active .onion routing across web, worker, node, SDK CLI, extension,
  publish-action, and WordPress plugin for the AWS node deployment
- Ensure backwards compatibility with existing v1 SDK clients and unauthenticated
  community-node callers (accept valid v1 signatures as legacy alongside v2;
  use optionalScope on publish/raw, upload, bridge, and webhook routes unless
  REQUIRE_API_KEY=true; preserve non-null ipfsUrl/gatewayUrl and webhook response
  fields)
- Resolve CodeQL clear-text storage alerts (#153, #154, #155) by keeping
  encrypted key records inside IndexedDB and writing only public metadata to
  localStorage
- Resolve CodeQL missing-rate-limiting alerts (#156-#160) by registering
  @fastify/rate-limit globally and caching Tor hostname discovery outside
  request handlers
- Fix CI action SHAs in sdk-conformance job and enable loopback webhook test
  delivery in test-webhook-subscriptions.ts
docs(deploy): Note required fly secrets for node operators

feat(node): harden sovereign community node for first deployment

Infrastructure & persistence:
- Persistent Ed25519 node identity (DATA_DIR/identity), surfaced in status
- Embedded JSON store fallback when DATABASE_URL is unset, with a
  Prisma-shaped compat layer so routes/services work in sovereign mode
- Helia fs blockstore/datastore + stable libp2p peer key under DATA_DIR
- Unified content cache under DATA_DIR; atomic JSON stores for API keys
  and webhook subscriptions
- Repo-root Dockerfile via pnpm deploy --legacy (vendors workspace SDK),
  persistent /data volume incl. Tor hidden-service keys; fly/render/
  compose contexts updated

Auth & scoping:
- No hardcoded admin key: bootstrap via ADMIN_API_KEY or generated key
- Scoped keys (publish:raw/publish:signed/resolve/pin/federate/admin)
  gate operator routes: federation peers/policy/gated, admin keys,
  uploads, bridge medium/substack/cms, publish/raw
- Signed publish requires protocol v2; v1 rejected with legacy notice
- /api/v1/verify returns verified/legacy/invalid status

Federation & webhooks:
- Gossip verifies the content-bound signature against fetched content;
  unsigned gossip rejected by default; timing-safe PSK; whitelists
- Webhook subs authenticated, owner-scoped, SSRF-validated at create and
  delivery; secret returned only at creation
- Ghost/Strapi ingress requires configured env secrets (raw-body HMAC,
  constant-time compare); bridge keys can no longer be caller-supplied

Honesty:
- Storage reports 'local' vs 'ipfs' tier; no fake ipfs:// URLs when
  content was only written to the local store
- Tor reader sanitizes article HTML, escapes metadata, sends CSP, and
  shows a real verification result instead of a decorative badge
- All generated URLs use PUBLIC_NODE_URL / PUBLIC_APP_URL

Tests: fastify.inject route suite (13), federated suites updated for
signed gossip; CI gains node/worker/route suites + SDK conformance job

feat(protocol): Content-bound v2 signatures across all signers and SDKs (#152, #167)

Signatures previously covered only {title, tags, timestamp}, so an article body
could be swapped while keeping a valid signature, and readers accepted even
title-only signatures. Every signer now produces protocol v2 signatures: Ed25519
over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {proto, title, tags, timestamp, contentSha256}.
Verifiers report v2 as "verified" and v1 as "legacy (metadata only)", never
verified; title-only candidates are gone.

- web: editor, proof export and API explorer sign v2; reader/embed/provenance UI
  show the legacy state; verification delegates to @pressprotocol/sdk/protocol
- importers (URL, Notion, bulk RSS) sign in the browser via a shared helper; the
  server import routes no longer accept private keys (also fixes the URL import
  preview, which read a field the API never returned)
- SDK client/CLI, widget, browser extension (previously key-sorted v1 that never
  verified) and publish action sign v2; proof decoder reports legacy signatures
- WordPress: signs locally with libsodium; the key is generated on first use,
  stored encrypted with a key derived from the SECURE_AUTH salt, and migrated from
  the old plaintext option; private keys are no longer sent to the API; tags are
  sent as a JSON list
- worker: a public key without a signature is treated as unsigned
- Python, Go and Rust SDKs implement v2 signing/verification
- spec/test-vectors/signature-v2.json: shared conformance vectors (valid,
  tampered, legacy) verified by TS, Python, Go, Rust and PHP implementations

deps(web): Upgrade to Next.js 15.5.28 and React 19; remove unused auth stack (#154)

Next.js 14.1 (and the whole 14.2 line) carries unpatched critical advisories; all
Next.js/React advisories are resolved on 15.5.28 + React 19.3.1. Migration:

- async route/page params and searchParams (Next 15 request APIs)
- serverComponentsExternalPackages -> serverExternalPackages
- outputFileTracingRoot set to the monorepo root
- React 19 ref typings in reader components
- dompurify 3.4.17 (security fixes); drop deprecated @types/dompurify

Removes code that was never called by the app: the hand-rolled SIWE/JWT login
routes (/api/auth/login, /api/auth/validate, /api/protected, /api/user/check),
the middleware that forwarded a user header to them, and the unused
wagmi/viem/react-query/RainbowKit providers and siwe/jsonwebtoken deps. Privy
remains the single auth provider; embed framing headers now come solely from
next.config.js.

fix: Report real telemetry instead of placeholder values (#162)

- worker /api/manifests/stats returned hardcoded counts (142/38/45); it now
  derives totals, unique tags and publishers from the content index and returns
  null with source "unavailable" when no index is attached
- worker status/metrics no longer claim a PoP count
- node status reports the real Helia peer id/peer count (null/0 when Helia is not
  running) and only reports the DHT active when it has peers
- node no longer reports a fixed 450 ms onion latency; latency is null until it
  is actually measured

fix(worker): Add input validation, body size caps and rate limiting (#164)

The edge API pinned anything it received to the project's Pinata account with no
limits. Now:

- zod schemas for /api/content and /api/v1/publish/* (title <= 500 chars,
  body <= 1 MiB, <= 20 tags, hex-validated keys/signatures, parseable timestamps);
  title/body are validated without being mutated so signatures still match
- 2 MiB JSON and ~10 MiB upload body limits (413)
- image uploads restricted to PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/AVIF
- CID validation before any gateway fan-out on :cid routes
- Cloudflare Rate Limiting bindings: 10 publishes/min and 120 reads/min per IP
  (no-op when the binding is absent, e.g. local dev)

fix: Disable Tor routes until a node hidden service is deployed (#153)

Tor mirrors are served by the PressProtocol node, which is not deployed yet, but
every surface advertised a placeholder .onion host that is not a valid v3 address
(including an Onion-Location header on every web page). Tor is now advertised only
when a real 56-character v3 address is configured (NEXT_PUBLIC_TOR_ONION_HOST,
TOR_ONION_GATEWAY, TOR_ONION_ADDRESS):

- web: no Onion-Location header or Tor mirror by default; reader shows
  "Tor Onion Mirror — coming soon"
- worker: omits mirrors.tor / Onion-Location; placeholder removed from wrangler.toml
- node: no fabricated dev onion; configured and on-disk hosts are validated
- extension, SDK CLI, publish action, WordPress plugin: Tor links only when configured

Also drops the unrelated content-route header comment churn from the proxy fix.

fix(worker): Verify Ed25519 signatures at the edge; add shared signature protocol

/api/v1/verify reported every input as verified and /api/v1/publish/signed pinned
without checking signatures. Both now verify for real, as does /api/content when a
key/signature is supplied; invalid signatures return 401 and unsigned content is
labelled unsigned instead of carrying placeholder keys. /api/v1/resolve reports
the actual verification status, and /api/v1/publish/raw signs with the operator
key only when EDGE_SIGNING_KEY is configured.

Adds @pressprotocol/sdk/protocol as the single implementation of signing and
verification: v2 signs an RFC 8785 canonical payload that binds the body via
SHA-256; v1 (metadata-only) signatures verify as "legacy", never "verified".
Title and body are no longer trimmed after signing.

feat(web,extension): Seal burner private keys at rest (#165)

Burner identities no longer store the raw Ed25519 private key in localStorage or
chrome.storage. The key is sealed with AES-GCM under a non-extractable CryptoKey
held in IndexedDB; public fields stay readable for UI. Existing plaintext entries
are migrated transparently on next load, with plaintext only as a fallback where
WebCrypto/IndexedDB are unavailable. Profile key import now uses the same path and
async key derivation.

fix(web): Sanitize untrusted article HTML and add baseline security headers

Article bodies resolve from arbitrary CIDs, so every dangerouslySetInnerHTML path
(reader, embed, import and Notion previews, editor preview) now goes through one
DOMPurify-based sanitizer that strips scripts, handlers, forms, frames and inline
styles, hardens links and images, and never emits markup during SSR.

Adds nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options
for non-embed routes, and object-src/base-uri restrictions everywhere.

fix(web): Return 502 when content backends are unreachable (#155)

The publish proxy swallowed upstream failures, so its fallback branch never ran
and the handler returned no response. Retry only on 5xx/network errors, pass 4xx
through, and fail with an explicit 502. Dedicated IPFS gateway settings are now
read from environment configuration in both the web app and the edge worker, and
CIDs are validated before gateway fan-out.

ci: Dependency audit job + self-hosted fonts (fix flaky web builds)

fix(web): Declare variable font weight ranges for local fonts

next/font/local does not inspect font files, so omitting the weight
option emits @font-face without a font-weight descriptor — clamping the
variable fonts to weight 400 and forcing faux-bold synthesis for
semibold/bold text. Declare the actual wght ranges (Inter 100-900,
Source Serif 4 200-900, JetBrains Mono 100-800) verified from each
file's fvar table.

ci: Add dependency audit job and self-host fonts to fix flaky builds

- Add non-blocking `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` job to CI; flip to
  blocking once issue #65 is resolved.
- Replace next/font/google with next/font/local for Inter, Source Serif 4,
  Instrument Serif, and JetBrains Mono. The build-time Google Fonts fetch
  was the root cause of intermittent "Validate Web Portal" failures on
  unrelated PRs, and self-hosting removes a build-time network dependency
  (and any runtime font-request surface) entirely.

Merge pull request #111 from 0xshikhar/feat/security-sanitization-fixes

Feat/security fixes

refactor: Refine content excerpt generation and update Rails test

This commit includes two minor refinements: In `scrubber.ts`, the content excerpt generation logic is cleaned up by removing redundant `|| description` fallbacks after `cheerio.load(...).text()`. `cheerio.load(...).text()` already returns an empty string if no text is found, making the fallback unnecessary and simplifying the code. In `test-universal-rails.ts`, a test assertion for the `torproject` URL is updated to include the `https://` prefix, making the assertion more precise and robust.

fix: Harden Obsidian plugin regexes to prevent ReDoS

This commit updates the regular expressions used in the Obsidian plugin for parsing wiki-links and embedded transclusions. The previous regexes could be vulnerable to Regex Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks with crafted long inputs. The updated regexes include explicit length limits (e.g., `{1,300}`) to mitigate this risk, improving the plugin's resilience and preventing potential performance degradation or crashes when processing malformed or excessively long link syntax.

fix: Improve privacy scanner and URL sanitization

This commit enhances the privacy scanning utility and URL sanitization within the browser extension. The `scanContentPrivacy` function in `privacy-scanner.ts` now uses the `URL` object for more robust and accurate detection of surveillance domains, reducing false negatives compared to regex-only approaches. The browser extension's `sanitizeUrl` function is strengthened to explicitly purge `javascript:` and `data:` URIs earlier in the process, preventing potential XSS vectors. An additional check for the `srcdoc` attribute in iframes is added to prevent potential XSS through embedded content.

fix: Enhance HTML/Markdown sanitization and parsing logic

This commit refines several areas of content processing to improve security and parsing accuracy. The `stripHtmlTags` function in `SovereignMirrorService` and the `widget` package is rewritten for safer, character-level stripping, mitigating potential XSS bypasses that could occur with `DOMParser` or simpler regex approaches. The `extractTitle` function in `widget.js` now avoids `DOMParser` for robustness and includes attribute sanitization within its regex-based `<h1>` extraction. Markdown callout parsing in `notion.ts` and `publisher.ts` is made more resilient to various emoji representations, including handling Unicode variation selectors. Inline markdown rendering in `publisher.ts` now explicitly replaces `on[a-zA-Z]` event handlers with a `data-purged` attribute, providing a clearer indication of sanitization.
chore: Pin Rust toolchain to stable in publish-ecosystem workflow
ci: Include security branch in CodeQL and Scorecard workflows
Merge branch 'master' into feat/security-sanitization-fixes

fix(security): improve markdown escaping and script purging in publish action

This commit enhances the `publish-action` integration to improve the security of markdown processing. The `escapeMarkdown` function in `index.ts` is updated to escape a broader set of characters (`<`, `>`, `[`, `]`, `` ` ``) that could be used for injection attacks or markdown rendering issues.

Additionally, `publisher.ts` now includes an explicit check to purge executable script tags during markdown transpilation, removing a less robust post-processing regex replacement. This ensures that any embedded scripts are removed early in the processing pipeline, further mitigating XSS risks.

fix(security): sanitize cache file paths to prevent directory traversal

This commit introduces path sanitization to the `StorageService` when reading from and writing to the content cache. Specifically, `path.basename` and `path.resolve` are used in conjunction with a `startsWith` check to ensure that cache file paths are strictly confined within the intended cache directory.

This prevents potential directory traversal vulnerabilities where a malicious actor could craft a CID value containing path manipulation sequences (e.g., `../`) to access or write to arbitrary locations on the file system.

fix(security): enhance HTML tag stripping to prevent XSS

This commit refactors the HTML tag stripping logic in several key areas to use a more robust character-by-character parsing approach instead of regular expressions. Regex-based stripping can be vulnerable to bypasses and edge cases, potentially leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities.

The new implementation iterates through the HTML string, maintaining a state to determine if the current character is inside an HTML tag. This ensures that only actual text content is extracted, significantly improving the security of content sanitization.

chore(deps): pin GitHub Actions to specific SHAs

This commit updates all GitHub Actions used across various workflows to their specific commit SHAs instead of mutable tags (e.g., `v4`). This practice enhances security by preventing unexpected changes in action behavior if a tag is updated by the action maintainer, and improves reproducibility of builds.

Each action is now referenced by its full SHA, ensuring that the exact version of the action that was tested and approved is always used.

test(testing): Update CMS scrubber and universal Rails tests

Updates existing test scripts for the CMS scrubber and universal Rails integration, ensuring comprehensive test coverage for recent changes or new features.

chore(publish-action): Update action entry point

Adjusts the main entry point for the publish GitHub Action, potentially for dependency updates or minor configuration changes.

feat(privacy-scanner): feat(privacy): Implement privacy scanning utility

Introduces a new utility for scanning and identifying privacy-sensitive information within content, enhancing data protection capabilities.

refactor(obsidian-plugin): refactor(obsidian): Update Obsidian plugin structure

Updates the core structure and logic of the Obsidian plugin, potentially for better maintainability or compatibility.

refactor(browser-extension): refactor(extension): Improve content handling in browser extension

feat(web): Implement resilient multi-transport content retrieval

The `ApiClient`'s `getContent` method has been updated to leverage this new proxy route. It first attempts to fetch from the primary backend with a timeout. If that fails or is slow, it falls back to querying the local Next.js `/api/content/[cid]` proxy, which then handles the multi-transport logic.
